source: Dungeons & Dividends rulebook, Draft v1, as supplied by the repo owner. Sections cited per entry. This file is a transcription of that document, not an interpretation of it.
confidenceNote: A house game system, not a financial standard. Nothing here is advice; the mechanics are a lens on numbers computed elsewhere in the suite.
note: Rulebook content only. Every dollar-to-score threshold lives in dnd_scoring.json instead, because those were NOT specified by the rulebook (its Section 13 item 3 says so explicitly) and were agreed separately. Keeping them apart means a scoring recalibration never edits transcribed rules.

stats.name: Strength
stats.measures: Raw income, career capital, and your capacity to earn — nothing else
stats.save: A sudden need to out-earn a problem (income shock, needing a side hustle fast)

stats.name: Dexterity
stats.measures: How easily you can move out of the way of a hit — job loss, needing to relocate, needing to unwind debt fast
stats.save: Getting stuck — job loss, forced relocation, needing to unwind a bad position quickly

stats.name: Constitution
stats.measures: Your ability to sustain a savings rate over time without breaking
stats.save: Lifestyle inflation eating your savings rate under stress or a windfall

stats.name: Intelligence
stats.measures: Technical financial literacy — tax law, account types, market history, terminology
stats.save: A technical mistake — tax error, misunderstanding a contract, misreading a rule

stats.name: Wisdom
stats.measures: Ability to model consequences before acting, plus how honestly you know your own patterns around money
stats.save: A scam, a get-rich-quick pitch, or a decision you'd regret if you modeled it out first

stats.name: Charisma
stats.measures: Ability to change your terms in the world, who you can call on, and how well you bring people along with you
stats.save: Social-pressure spending — keeping up with peers, guilt-driven lending

subStats.name: Income Power
subStats.measures: Raw earning capacity relative to your role/market right now

subStats.name: Income Trajectory
subStats.measures: Growth trend — raises, promotions, career capital compounding over time

subStats.name: Hustle Capacity
subStats.measures: Ability to stand up additional income on demand

subStats.name: Liquidity Agility
subStats.measures: How fast you can get to usable cash without a penalty

subStats.name: Structural Mobility
subStats.measures: Housing and geographic flexibility — rent vs own, remote portability, willingness to move

subStats.name: Obligation Flexibility
subStats.measures: How easily your fixed costs and debts can be restructured or shed

subStats.name: Consistency
subStats.measures: Track record of sustaining that rate through disruption, not just in a good year

subStats.name: Reserve Depth
subStats.measures: Actual buffer size — emergency fund months, cushion beyond the bare minimum

subStats.name: Tax Literacy
subStats.measures: Understanding of the tax code and how to legally optimize against it

subStats.name: Market/Historical Literacy
subStats.measures: Understanding of market cycles, risk/return, and financial history

subStats.name: Instrument Literacy
subStats.measures: Understanding of specific vehicles — account types, insurance products, loan structures

subStats.name: Scenario Foresight
subStats.measures: Ability to model consequences and run scenarios before acting

subStats.name: Self-Awareness & Discipline
subStats.measures: How honestly you know your own spending triggers, and the patience to act on it

subStats.name: Threat Detection
subStats.measures: Ability to smell a bad deal or predatory pitch before it lands

subStats.name: Negotiation
subStats.measures: Ability to change terms in your favor — salary, rates, fee waivers, contracts

subStats.name: Network
subStats.measures: Breadth and quality of relationships that create financial opportunity

subStats.name: Personability
subStats.measures: Ability to get people around you genuinely aligned, not just compliant

levelBands.milestone: Debt Burden stabilizing, starter emergency fund built
Full emergency fund, employer match captured, Roth IRA active

armor.label: Emergency fund
armor.note: Rulebook §3A names +2 explicitly. Requires the reserve to reach the conventional 3-month floor.

armor.label: Health insurance
armor.note: §3A says it 'scales with coverage quality' without numbers. Bands agreed with the owner: none 0, high-deductible 1, standard 2, low-deductible/rich 3.

armor.label: Disability insurance
armor.note: §3A: 'the one that protects your STR (income) directly'. Value agreed, not stated in the rulebook.

armor.label: Umbrella liability
armor.note: §3A: 'built for the single biggest possible hit'. Value agreed, not stated in the rulebook.

armor.label: Diversification across Classes
armor.note: §3A: 'a proficiency bonus that compounds with all the above rather than replacing them'. Applies when two or more classes are actively played.

debtBurden.effect: Disadvantage on CON saves against lifestyle inflation — little room to save aggressively while servicing debt
Max HP reduced by 25% (interest eats directly into runway); locks multiclassing into investing classes per §5A

debtBurden.trigger: Multiple high-interest balances straining the budget
debtBurden.effect: AC reduced; disadvantage on DEX saves
Credit damage — AC further reduced; disadvantage on any check involving borrowing
Merges directly into the Death Saves mechanic (§3A) as the terminal state

triageTechniques.name: Avalanche Triage
triageTechniques.detail: Target the highest-APR balance first. The best save bonus against the single largest balance; mathematically optimal, slowest visible first win.

triageTechniques.name: Snowball Triage
triageTechniques.detail: Target the smallest balance first. A smaller save bonus, but success grants temporary Inspiration — behavioral momentum modeled as a real mechanic.

triageTechniques.name: Consolidation Triage
triageTechniques.detail: Merge balances into one instrument. A one-time reduction of a full Debt Burden Level on success, but future incremental saves against the consolidated balances stop.

universalDebtFeats.name: The No-Spend Month
universalDebtFeats.detail: Once per Long Rest, temporarily double Triage progress by suppressing discretionary spending for one cycle.

universalDebtFeats.name: The Side Hustle Surge
universalDebtFeats.detail: Direct all Hustle Capacity income straight at Triage.

universalDebtFeats.name: Balance Transfer Master
universalDebtFeats.detail: Chain multiple 0%-APR offers without the usual credit-score AC penalty.

generalFeats.name: The Ask
generalFeats.detail: Successfully negotiate a raise or rate; grants a permanent STR bonus.

generalFeats.name: Lucky
generalFeats.detail: Reroll one failed save per Long Rest.

generalFeats.name: Tough
generalFeats.detail: +2 Max HP per level, retroactively — a deliberately built emergency fund, not a passive trait.

generalFeats.name: Mobile
generalFeats.detail: Relocate for a job or cost-of-living arbitrage without a resilience check.

featTrees.name: Protection Feats
featTrees.blurb: Levels up the AC layer in §3A. Its whole job is preventing a hit from landing at all, not recovering after one does.

feats.name: The Income Shield
feats.detail: Life and disability coverage in place; converts what would be a full STR loss from The Sudden Ability Drain into a partial, recoverable one.

feats.name: The Property Shield
feats.detail: Home, auto, and umbrella coverage; AC bonus against Monster and Hazard hits that target assets directly.

feats.name: The Long-Term Care Ward
feats.detail: Built specifically against the Medical Bankruptcy Behemoth hazard.

featTrees.name: Tax Strategy Feats
featTrees.blurb: Shows up as reduced Revenue Guild damage across whatever class you're actually playing, not as HP or Level of its own.

feats.name: Entity Architect
feats.detail: LLC/S-corp structuring; most synergistic with The Builder.

feats.name: Account Optimizer
feats.detail: Sequencing across account types (backdoor Roth, mega backdoor, asset location); most synergistic with The Compounder and The Anchor.

feats.name: The Multi-State/International Strategist
feats.detail: Residency and jurisdiction arbitrage; pairs naturally with The Keeper's Geoarbitrageur.

featTrees.name: Legacy & Giving Feats
featTrees.blurb: The 'beyond yourself' tree. Genuinely easy to ignore, since most people don't reach for it until they're forced to.

feats.name: Legacy Storyteller
feats.detail: The non-financial transfer: values, an ethical will, the story behind the money.

feats.name: The Direct Giver
feats.detail: Cash giving, mutual aid, immediate impact.

feats.name: The Structured Giver
feats.detail: Donor-Advised Funds, Qualified Charitable Distributions, tax-efficient vehicles.

feats.name: The Founder
feats.detail: Founding or funding an organization directly; most adjacent to The Builder.

monsters.name: Lifestyle-Inflation Imp
monsters.note: Small, constant, everywhere — the 'just this once' purchase

monsters.name: Payday Loan Wraith
monsters.note: Preys on people already cornered; compounds fast

monsters.name: Commission Churn-Wraith
monsters.note: The advisor who believes in the product but is paid to sell it to you

monsters.name: Timeshare Charm-Caster
monsters.note: Bypasses AC entirely — a Charm effect on judgment, not a physical hit

monsters.name: Whole-Life-Insurance Basilisk
monsters.note: Sold with real concern for your family — still locks up liquidity you needed

hazards.name: Market Crash Elemental
hazards.damage: Paper Level loss only converts to real HP damage if the WIS save is failed
hazards.note: Not malicious — a weather event. The save is about your reaction, not the event

hazards.name: Inflation Wraith
hazards.damage: 1d4/month, ongoing — chip damage that never stops on its own
hazards.note: Ambient, not a single strike; the danger is treating a 'safe' allocation as immune

hazards.name: Divorce Dragon
hazards.note: A true boss fight — attacks every stat at once

hazards.name: The Dual-Income Collapse
hazards.note: Triggers when a household depending on two incomes loses one

hazards.name: Medical Bankruptcy Behemoth
hazards.damage: 12d10, often triggers the Massive Damage Rule if uninsured
hazards.note: Scales with how thin your insurance (AC) actually is

hazards.name: The Sudden Ability Drain
hazards.note: An injury or illness event that triggers the Disabled status effect directly

revenueGuild.blurb: The tax system is a Faction, not a Monster: a lawful, rules-based organization with its own ranks and its own win condition (compliance), not a hunger for your money specifically.

ladder.rank: The Ledger (a trap, not an NPC)
ladder.trigger: Runs automatically on every filed return
ladder.defense: Accurate filing is the ward that keeps the trap from triggering at all

ladder.onFail: Small tax bill; interest starts as ongoing poison damage until resolved

ladder.trigger: A claimed deduction or credit needs paper backup
ladder.onFail: Deduction denied + back tax if you can't produce the document

ladder.trigger: Multiple flags, unusually large deductions, or a random pull
ladder.onFail: Multi-year reassessment, penalties, possible referral upward
ladder.defense: An Enrolled Agent or CPA companion fighting the encounter for you

ladder.trigger: Auditor's findings escalated for supervisor sign-off
ladder.onFail: Formal Notice of Deficiency — real money now at stake
ladder.defense: A tax attorney companion; your right to invoke Appeals

ladder.trigger: Auditor suspects a willful, intentional pattern — not an honest mistake
ladder.onFail: Boss-tier. A different game entirely (criminal, not civil)
ladder.defense: Nothing here meaningfully saves you — the meta-strategy is never triggering it

revenueGuild.neutralGround: Appeals and Tax Court aren't encounters — they're an arena you can invoke instead of accepting the Department's ruling. It costs resources (usually a companion) but resets the outcome to a fresh judgment.
revenueGuild.standing: Faction Standing is a separate meter from your six stats. Round-number deductions, home-office claims, a cash-heavy business, and aggressive Schedule C losses lower it. Clean multi-year history, consistent numbers, and e-filing raise it.

allies.name: Enrolled Agent
allies.detail: Licensed specifically to represent you before this Faction; advantage at Tier 3

allies.name: Tax Attorney
allies.detail: Required at Tier 4+; the only ally who can invoke privilege, a ward that blocks certain information from being compelled

statusEffects.name: Unemployed (Collecting)
statusEffects.trigger: Job loss, filed for Unemployment Insurance
statusEffects.grants: A recurring Short-Rest-style HP source (the weekly benefit)
statusEffects.restricts: Cannot multiclass into The Builder in most states while collecting; weekly job-search check; must accept a 'suitable work' encounter or forfeit
statusEffects.duration: State-dependent, commonly ~26 weeks; ends early on new income, or decays into Exhausted

statusEffects.name: Disabled (Government Disability)
statusEffects.grants: A long-term recurring income stream; often bundled health coverage (an AC boost)
statusEffects.restricts: A hard STR ceiling — earning above the program limit triggers reduction or loss; assets above a threshold can disqualify entirely
statusEffects.duration: Indefinite, subject to a periodic Continuing Disability Review

statusEffects.name: Discharged (Post-Bankruptcy)
statusEffects.grants: Most prior debt wiped — a Restoration effect on HP
statusEffects.restricts: AC penalty (damaged credit) lasting 7–10 years; long cooldown before reuse
statusEffects.duration: Long, fixed; fades as the credit-damage penalty tapers

statusEffects.name: Full-Time Student
statusEffects.grants: Federal loan interest/payments paused — temporary immunity to Debt-class monster damage on those loans
statusEffects.restricts: STR penalty — capped hours; XP toward The Earner slows
statusEffects.duration: Ends at graduation or dropping below half-time

statusEffects.name: W-2 Employee
statusEffects.grants: Employer 401(k) match (a passive buff) and employer-sponsored insurance (AC)
statusEffects.restricts: Less control over Hustle Capacity income timing
statusEffects.duration: Ends on job change or reclassification

statusEffects.name: 1099 / Self-Employed
statusEffects.grants: Solo 401(k)/SEP IRA with far higher contribution limits
statusEffects.restricts: Self-employment tax (an ongoing STR tax); no employer match; higher Revenue Guild encounter odds if quarterlies are underpaid

statusEffects.name: Underwater / Negative Equity
statusEffects.restricts: Restrained on The Landholder — can't sell without bringing cash to closing; Structural Mobility treated as near-zero

statusEffects.name: Means-Tested Benefit
statusEffects.restricts: The Benefits Cliff — cross the line and the entire benefit can vanish at once
statusEffects.duration: Ends when income/assets cross the threshold

benefitsCliff: Several statuses don't taper. Cross the income or asset line by even a small amount and the whole benefit can vanish — a small raise costing far more in lost benefits than it provides. It plays like a trap dealing damage proportional to the benefit lost, not the size of the trigger, and it is exactly what Scenario Foresight exists to see coming.

outcomes: 3 successes → Stabilized. HP resets to 1. You found a way out — sold something, borrowed, cut spending hard.
3 failures → Insolvency. Forced bankruptcy or default. Not game over, but it costs Level and leaves a lasting debuff.
Natural 20 equivalent (an unexpected windfall while at 0) → instantly stabilize and regain 1 HP.
Natural 1 equivalent (a second crisis while already down) → counts as two failures.
A Companion (bankruptcy attorney, debt counselor, a family member able to lend) can auto-stabilize you once.
deathSaves.massiveDamage: If a single hit deals damage equal to or greater than your Max HP in one shot, you skip death saves entirely and go straight to Insolvency. This is why AC (insurance) matters more than raw HP against the biggest monsters.
recovery: Short Rest (a pay cycle) — regain HP equal to (income − expenses) for that cycle, if positive.
Long Rest (a strong, uninterrupted month or quarter) — regain HP up to max, contingent on a CON save.
Potion (a windfall) — heals a fixed amount immediately, no rest required.
deathSaves.temporaryHp: A windfall sitting in checking that hasn't been moved into real reserves. Absorbs the next hit first, doesn't stack with itself, and evaporates at your next Long Rest if not converted into permanent HP.
